newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-VICENZA GO TOP TO MAKE SERIE A HISTORY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VICENZA GO TOP TO MAKE SERIE A HISTORY.

text.p: Unsung striker Gabriele Ambrosetti made serie A history on Sunday, scoring twice in Vicenza's 2-0 win over Reggiana to leave his side outright leaders of the Italian championship for the first time.
He turned home Marcelo Otero's cross in the 34th minute for Vicenza's opener before clinching his side's great day with a second midway through the second half.
But Ambrosetti's and Vicenza's taste of glory would be shortlived if Internazionale, leaders at the start of the day, beat champions Milan in their evening derby.

Vicenza, who briefly shared the serie A lead in 1963 but have never enjoyed an outright lead in their 94-year history, top the table with 20 points from 10 matches, one ahead of Bologna, 3-1 winners over Atalanta, and two in front of Inter.
"The title is beyond our ambitions," said manager Francesco Guidolin, "but we're going to enjoy this moment of history for a few hours."
Bologna, who won their last league title in 1964, made light work of Atalanta once Davide Fortunato deflected Cristiano Scapolo's cross past his own goalkeeper in the 22nd minute.
In the 55th minute a first-time shot from Russian Igor Kolyvanov, lurking on the edge of the area, made it 2-0 before Pierpaolo Bresciani added a third three minutes later.
Bologna could even afford the luxury of Scapolo's missed penalty in the 65th minute before Felippo Inzaghi added respectability to the scoreline with his eighth goal of the season.
Inzaghi, signed from Parma in the close season, is now joint top scorer in serie A with Roma's Abel Balbo.

European champions Juventus, who are in Tokyo for next week's Intercontinental Cup against Argentina's River Plate, lie equal fourth on 16 points with Napoli, who needed a last-minute goal from Fabio Pecchia to draw 1-1 at Cagliari.
In the closest title race in years, three teams -- Sampdoria, Roma and Perugia -- lie equal sixth on 15 points.
Sampdoria were left to rue the 80th minute dismissal of defender Emanuele Pesaresi for a second yellow card in their 1-1 draw with Lazio at the Olympic stadium.
Within a minute of Pesaresi's dismissal the unmarked Paolo Negro equalised Roberto Mancini's fifth minute goal for the visitors -- a well-judged header for his 131st career goal.

Roma's scoreless draw at struggling Parma was noteworthy only for the debut of the visitors' Daniele Conti -- the 17-year-old son of Bruno Conti, who was a key member of Italy's 1982 World Cup winning side.

Perugia's long suffering manager Giovanni Galeone, living on a knife's edge since falling out with his president Luciano Gaucci in the close season, prolonged his managerial life for another week with a 3-1 home win over struggling Verona. CJE
